claims.text: Applying a thin, dense refractory nitride coating by PVD to high-value alloy surfaces will improve their surface physical and mechanical properties in aggressive environments.
PVD sputtering or evaporation can form a dense, adherent refractory nitride thin film.
The intervention forms a uniform, hard nitride layer.
The nitride layer acts as a barrier to chemical attack.
The nitride layer acts as a barrier to wear.
The nitride coating reduces local stress concentration and surface degradation.
A refractory nitride coating enhances surface hardness and chemical inertness.
The coating's dense structure impedes diffusion of aggressive species into the substrate.
Improved coating-mediated wear resistance reduces mechanical damage during cyclic or sliding contact.
Compared with untreated specimens, coated components will have increased surface hardness.
Compared with untreated specimens, coated components will have lower wear rates.
Compared with untreated specimens, coated components will have improved corrosion resistance.
The coating is expected to remain effective at 200–300°C in chloride- or acid-containing environments under simultaneous wear loading.
The intervention remains effective only while coating adhesion and integrity are maintained.
Extreme mechanical stress, temperatures beyond the coating's stability range, or prolonged chemical exposure can degrade the coating.
The effectiveness of the intervention may depend on coating thickness and PVD process parameters.
